newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson Q2 above target - Goldman Sachs.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson Q2 above target - Goldman Sachs.

text.p: SGS-Thomson Microelectronics' second-quarter 1997 profit was slightly better than expected but full year estimates may have to be reduced, Goldman Sachs analyst Charles Elliott said.
Earlier today the company reported that first half net income fell to $182.6 million from $351.1 million, while second quarter net income fell to $92.1 million from $176.1 million.
Elliott said the market consensus for 1998 earnings per share of more than $5.0 was still very reasonable.
Elliot said in a phone interview after a company presentation in Paris that the share was currently undervalued.
STM's stock was down 1.07 percent at 555 francs at 1100 GMT. In New York it closed at $93 after a very strong run recently.
"I still believe that the true value of the stock is $105," he said.
"The second quarter was slightly better than expected. I expected (earnings per share of) 62 cents, the market average was 65 cents and they delivered 66 cents," he told Reuters.
"The full year consensus is $3.50 and that seems a little bit high now that recovery will start in the fourth quarter and not in the third," Elliott said.
"But the next year consensus of $5.0 plus is still very reasonable," he said.
